text:
Alex Martin: Quick sync — ACME POC. Need to lock success criteria, SE coverage, timeline, and outstanding security Qs. I'm proposing a 4–6 week focused run with 2 SE touchpoints.
Samir Patel: +1. Can you share the proposed success metrics? throughput/latency or qualitative evals?
Alex Martin: Primary goal = 90% intent classification accuracy on their 3 core flows (search, summarization, rerank). Secondary = <200ms median token latency for 95th pct on demo queries.
Monica Liu: For accuracy, do we have a prompt set and eval harness ready? We should run a dry eval before week 0.
Alex Martin: We have ~250 labeled examples from their PMs. Plan: run a baseline with current open model, then iterate with Redwood Optimize recommendations.
Ben Carter: Engineering ask — we'll need a SE for onboarding + one weekly deep-dive for prompt tuning. Can cover initial 2 weeks full-time then 4h/wk. Is that acceptable?
Samir Patel: That works. Resource-wise: SE = Ben (lead), DevX support = Monica for evals, and me for pricing/security liaise.
Alex Martin: Sounds good. Blockers: customer needs a completed security questionnaire and confirmation of data retention policy before we spin up Dedicated capacity.
Monica Liu: On the security Qs — we can provide a standard SAML/KMS answers doc but ACME asks about on-prem options. We'll need Private deployment RACI for the legal team.
Samir Patel: I'll escalate to legal. Timeline constraint from customer: must complete pilot acceptance by end of month 5 (their fiscal). That's 5 weeks away. Tight.
Alex Martin: Proposed compressed timeline (if we get security sign-off this week):
```
Week 0: kickoff, data ingest, baseline eval
Week 1: prompt tuning + model variants, SE deep-dive
Week 2: integrated app demo, perf tuning (batching/cache)
Week 3: final eval, customer shadow testing
Week 4: acceptance, handoff + cost/runbook docs
```
Ben Carter: Realistic if security Qs and sample data are provided by EOD Wed. Otherwise we need to push acceptance +2 weeks.
Casey-bot: Reminder: Created shared folder in Drive: /ACME_POC/ and scheduled recurring 30m status on Thursdays at 10am. :calendar:
Samir Patel: Pricing question from ACME — they want monthly committed capacity estimate vs pay-as-you-go. Can we produce a 3-tier estimate (dev/demo, pilot, production)?
Alex Martin: Yes. Monica — can you pull token/throughput numbers from baseline run so we can model costs?
Monica Liu: Will run baseline today and post numbers in the Drive. Also adding eval buckets: functional correctness (50%), hallucination/regression tests (30%), latency/cost (20%).
Ben Carter: Need to call out acceptance gates in the runbook: data/privacy sign-off, perf SLO, and quality bar (>=90% for core intents).
Alex Martin: Agreed. Final checklist to close before acceptance: security questionnaire signed, baseline eval report, demo recording, runbook with rollback plan, cost estimate.
Samir Patel: I'll own security questionnaire follow-up and legal loop. Ben = SE schedule + runbook. Monica = evals + numbers. Alex = customer sync and acceptance demo.
Monica Liu: Quick note — for prompts/evals we should capture top-10 failing examples for each iteration and include them in the regression suite.
Ben Carter: Can we get 2 cross-functional hours this week for an internal prep dry-run? Thursday 3pm?
Alex Martin: Thursday 3pm works for me. @Samir @Monica @Ben please confirm.
Samir Patel: Confirmed.
Monica Liu: Confirmed.
Ben Carter: Confirmed. :thumbsup:
Alex Martin: Great. If security sign-off arrives by Wed EOD we keep the compressed schedule. If not, I'll update ACME to plan +2 weeks.
Samir Patel: FYI — ACME's legal said they may need a SOC2 addendum; filing now.
Alex Martin: Thanks. I'll post an updated timeline after Wed. Short follow-ups only in this thread — please use the Drive folder for artifacts.
Samir Patel: Got it.
Casey-bot: Channel archived note will appear if thread inactive for 90 days.
